verdicts.verdictText: Laissez-faire, social democracy, state capitalism (for catch-up) — strong. Market socialism — strong on goods, weak on investment. Central planning — weak, with a strong negative record. Social anarchism — strong in mutualist form, untested otherwise. Anarcho-capitalism — strong on private goods, no answer for public ones. Parecon — untested; theoretically contested.

Laissez-faire, social democracy — strong. State capitalism — strong for catch-up, contested at the frontier. Market socialism — mixed. Central planning — weak outside priorities. Social anarchism, anarcho-capitalism, Parecon — untested.
Partly a value question. Market socialism, social anarchism, and Parecon eliminate the wage relation; social democracy moderates it; the others do not.
Parecon, social anarchism, market socialism — strongest by design, all scale-limited. Social democracy — moderate. Laissez-faire, anarcho-capitalism, central planning, state capitalism — weak.

Social democracy — strongest record. State capitalism — strong when willing, unaccountable when not. Market socialism — inherits social democracy's tools. Central planning — weak in practice. Social anarchism — local only. Laissez-faire, anarcho-capitalism — weak. Parecon — untested.

The structural solutions (market socialism, central planning, anarchism, Parecon) relocate concentration rather than eliminate it. Social democracy — mixed, erodes. State capitalism — concentrates in the state. Laissez-faire, anarcho-capitalism — weak.

Social democracy — strongest record, capture unresolved. State capitalism — depends on elite discipline, no guarantee. Anarchism and anarcho-capitalism — remove the target, no answer to re-emergence. Central planning — worst. Laissez-faire — weak by omission. Parecon — untested.

Social democracy — strongest. Laissez-faire, anarcho-capitalism — free formally, uneven in practice. State capitalism — free for citizens, restricted for migrants. Market socialism, social anarchism — admission-dependent. Central planning — worst. Parecon — untested.

Social democracy — strongest. State capitalism — effective where prioritized (Singapore housing), thin elsewhere. Central planning — unreliable. Market socialism — inherits social democracy. Laissez-faire, anarcho-capitalism — weak. Social anarchism — local. Parecon — untested.

verdicts.verdictText: Laissez-faire, central planning, state capitalism — scale by construction (with information loss). Social democracy — proven to ~100 million. Market socialism, social anarchism — bounded. Anarcho-capitalism, Parecon — unknown, with theoretical reasons for concern.
Social democracy — the only proven peaceful path. Laissez-faire — partial retrenchment only. Market socialism — one serious attempt, defeated. The rest — revolution, dictatorship, or no path.

Central planning and state capitalism — strongest, at civilian cost. Social democracy, market socialism, laissez-faire — conventional. Social anarchism — weakest with the clearest historical record. Anarcho-capitalism — theoretically unstable. Parecon — unaddressed.

Social democracy — strongest record. Social anarchism — strong at small scale (Ostrom), none at large. State capitalism — high variance, no guarantee. Market socialism — moderate. Laissez-faire, anarcho-capitalism — weak against dominant private actors. Central planning — worst. Parecon — partial by design, untested.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **▶ Acemoglu & Robinson — *The Narrow Corridor* (2019).** The strong-state-vs-strong-society framing; built around exactly the two-sided fear of private and state concentration.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Acemoglu & Robinson — *Why Nations Fail* (2012).** Inclusive vs. extractive institutions; why some countries stay in the corridor.
sourceSplits.reason: Bullet may describe multiple works or authors; review before splitting.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Buchanan & Tullock — *The Calculus of Consent* (1962).** Public choice: models officials as self-interested and asks which constitutional rules survive that assumption. The intellectual home of the government-tyranny worry.
sourceSplits.reason: Bullet may describe multiple works or authors; review before splitting.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Besley & Persson — *Pillars of Prosperity* (2011).** State capacity as a development achievement; why weak states are often more predatory.
sourceSplits.reason: Bullet may describe multiple works or authors; review before splitting.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Hall & Soskice (eds.) — *Varieties of Capitalism* (2001).** The "coordinated vs. liberal market economies" framework; the academic basis for treating Germany and the Nordics as a distinct system.
sourceSplits.reason: Bullet may describe multiple works or authors; review before splitting.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Hayek — *The Road to Serfdom* (1944)** and **Friedman — *Capitalism and Freedom* (1962).** The canonical statements of the taxation-and-tyranny worry; the laissez-faire side of the argument.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Whyte & Whyte — *Making Mondragon* (1988).** The definitive institutional history; explains the capital-account mechanics.

sourceSplits.rawMarkdown: **Michael Albert — *Parecon: Life After Capitalism* (2003).** Participatory economics; the main non-market democratic proposal.
